questions.answer: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. Velocity is required because a change of direction is also an acceleration.

option_feedback.A: Correct. This is the controlled definition of acceleration.
option_feedback.B: Speed has no direction, so this misses acceleration caused by a direction change.
option_feedback.C: Velocity multiplied by time has units of displacement, not acceleration.
option_feedback.D: Distance travelled per unit time defines speed.

questions.answer: Take east as positive. Delta v = 10.0 - 4.0 = 6.0 m s^-1. Acceleration = 6.0 / 3.0 = 2.0 m s^-2 east.

questions.answer: Both velocity and acceleration are negative, so both point west. When velocity and acceleration have the same direction, speed increases.

option_feedback.A: A negative velocity means west when east is positive.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Velocity and acceleration both point west, so the trolley speeds up westward.
option_feedback.C: The trolley does not move east, and opposite directions would be needed for slowing.
option_feedback.D: Negative acceleration does not automatically mean slowing. Here it has the same direction as velocity.
